executive_risk_memo: Aera V3 is an autonomous onchain treasury management protocol built by Gauntlet. Its control plane consists of a single BaseVaultFactory (0x29722cC9a1cACff4a15914F9bC274B46F3b90B4F) on Ethereum, owned by an OpenZeppelin TimelockController (0xce75E223E6DbB0503D2B6f55bC5907d1A0372E2B) with a 1-day minDelay. The factory uses a Solmate Auth contract (0xA83C037DF3b27bF7224AB0a40a2c4531FF1B2f40) as its authority, also owned by the same timelock. The timelock executed exactly one transaction (nonce=1): deploying the factory and authority in a single atomic operation. The factory has since created 45 vaults (nonce=45) across Ethereum, Base, Morph, Arbitrum, and Optimism. No EIP-1967 upgradeability, no multisig, no threshold governance - the entire control plane reduces to a single timelock with 1-day delay. The timelock admin is unknown (storage slot 0 empty), suggesting it may be a single EOA or the deployer. No public governance documentation exists on aera.finance, docs.aera.finance, or the aera-contracts-public GitHub repo. No Snapshot space or Tally proposals found. Engineering depth is minimal: 6 commits in 12 months (1 in v3/src), 2 contributors, bus factor 1. The main risk is concentration: a single timelock with unknown admin controls $151M TVL across 5 chains. No implementation upgrades have occurred since deployment (factory is immutable). Human researcher signoff confirmed; agent assistance via OpenCode.
